--- title: "pandas: loading and inspecting data" subtitle: "Session 6 · Topic 2.4 · Thu 10 Dec" format: revealjs --- ## Today ::: {.agenda} 1. Series and DataFrame 2. Reading CSV and Excel files 3. First look: `head`, `info`, `describe` 4. Selecting columns and rows: `[]`, `loc`, `iloc` 5. Filtering and sorting 6. New columns 7. Saving results ::: ## From NumPy to pandas NumPy: fast arrays, but columns have no names and one type for everything. pandas adds: - **named columns**, each with its own type (numbers, text, dates) - a **row index** (labels for rows) - reading / writing CSV, Excel, ...; handling missing values; grouping ::: {#3815279b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd import numpy as np pd.__version__ ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` '3.0.3' ``` ::: ::: ## Series: one labelled column ::: {#7c379b52 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} s = pd.Series([170.4, 527.5, 297.9], index=["R001", "R002", "R003"], name="max_stress_MPa") s ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` R001 170.4 R002 527.5 R003 297.9 Name: max_stress_MPa, dtype: float64 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#3973cb0c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} print(s["R002"], s.mean()) print(355 / s) # vectorised, like NumPy ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 527.5 331.93333333333334 R001 2.083333 R002 0.672986 R003 1.191675 Name: max_stress_MPa, dtype: float64 ``` ::: ::: ## DataFrame: a table ::: {#8cf79983 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} df_small = pd.DataFrame({ "thickness_mm": [17.3, 13.3, 18.3], "load_N": [1537, 2332, 2729], "max_stress_MPa": [170.4, 527.5, 297.9], }, index=["R001", "R002", "R003"]) df_small ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
thickness_mm load_N max_stress_MPa
R001 17.3 1537 170.4
R002 13.3 2332 527.5
R003 18.3 2729 297.9
``` ::: ::: - every column is a Series; they share the same index # Reading data {.divider} ## `read_csv` ::: {#034075d3 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} df = pd.read_csv("data/bracket.csv") df.head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

If numbers are text like `"12,5"`, the decimal sign is wrong. ::: # First look {.divider} ## Size and structure {.smaller} ::: {#22d1d299 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} print(df.shape) df.info(memory_usage=False) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` (300, 8) RangeIndex: 300 entries, 0 to 299 Data columns (total 8 columns): # Column Non-Null Count Dtype --- ------ -------------- ----- 0 run_id 300 non-null str 1 thickness_mm 300 non-null float64 2 fillet_radius_mm 300 non-null float64 3 load_N 300 non-null float64 4 E_GPa 300 non-null float64 5 max_stress_MPa 300 non-null float64 6 deflection_mm 300 non-null float64 7 safety_factor 300 non-null float64 dtypes: float64(7), str(1) ``` ::: ::: - `shape` → (rows, columns) - `info()` → column names, **types** (`dtype`), non-null counts, memory - first question for any new file: are the types what I expect? ## `describe`: summary statistics ::: {#edb494eb .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} df.describe().round(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}

ID column — unique? ::: {#562b1111 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} df["run_id"].is_unique ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=9} ``` True ``` ::: ::: # Selecting data {.divider} ## Columns ::: {#65dfe58e .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} df["max_stress_MPa"].head(3) # one column → Series ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ``` 0 170.4 1 527.5 2 297.9 Name: max_stress_MPa, dtype: float64 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#88c3b3fe .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} df[["thickness_mm", "load_N", "max_stress_MPa"]].head(3) # list → DataFrame ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=11} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {.muted} `df.max_stress_MPa` also works, but `df["..."]` always works (spaces, special characters). ::: ## Rows: `loc` (labels) and `iloc` (positions) ::: {#ef39b03a .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} runs = df.set_index("run_id") runs.loc["R002"] # one run by its label ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=12} ``` thickness_mm 13.300 fillet_radius_mm 1.900 load_N 2332.000 E_GPa 195.200 max_stress_MPa 527.500 deflection_mm 1.714 safety_factor 0.673 Name: R002, dtype: float64 ``` ::: ::: ## `loc` with ranges, `iloc` by position ::: {#3c66896d .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} runs.loc["R001":"R003", ["thickness_mm", "max_stress_MPa"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=13} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: # Changing data {.divider} ## New columns ::: {#ee823b73 .cell execution_count=19} ``` {.python .cell-code} df["nominal_stress_MPa"] = 6 * df["load_N"] * 150 / (40 * df["thickness_mm"] ** 2) df["Kt"] = df["max_stress_MPa"] / df["nominal_stress_MPa"] df["passes"] = df["safety_factor"] >= 1.5 df["E_MPa"] = df["E_GPa"] * 1000 df[["run_id", "nominal_stress_MPa", "Kt", "passes"]].head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=19} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: - column arithmetic is vectorised, like NumPy - `Kt` — stress concentration from the weld fillet, recovered from the data ## Renaming, dropping, apply ::: {#237a818a .cell execution_count=20} ``` {.python .cell-code} small = (df .rename(columns={"fillet_radius_mm": "r_mm"}) .drop(columns=["E_MPa"]) ) small["size_class"] = small["thickness_mm"].apply(lambda t: "thin" if t < 12 else "thick") small["size_class"].value_counts() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=20} ``` size_class thick 192 thin 108 Name: count, dtype: int64 ``` ::: ::: - methods return a **new** DataFrame — assign the result - `.apply(function)` for row-wise logic that is not simple arithmetic (slower) ## Saving ::: {#480939a0 .cell execution_count=21} ``` {.python .cell-code} df.to_csv("bracket_clean.csv", index=False) ``` ::: ```python df.to_excel("bracket.xlsx", index=False) # needs openpyxl df.to_parquet("bracket.parquet") # fast binary, keeps types ``` ## Your turn (25 min) ::: {.exercise} 1. Load `bracket.csv`; how many runs, which types, which ranges? 2. How many runs exceed yield (SF < 1)? What share is that? 3. Show the 5 runs with the **smallest** safety factor — which inputs do they have in common? 4. Add `nominal_stress_MPa` and `Kt`. Plot nothing yet — just check: is `Kt` larger for small or for large fillet radii? (Hint: compare means for `r < 3` and `r > 6`.) 5. Save runs with SF between 1 and 1.5 (borderline designs) to `borderline.csv`. ::: ## Summary - `pd.read_csv` with `sep`, `decimal`, `na_values`, `usecols`, `index_col` - first look: `shape`, `info()`, `describe()`, `head()` - `df["col"]`, `df[["a", "b"]]`, `loc` by label, `iloc` by position - filter with masks or `query`; sort with `sort_values` - new columns by vectorised arithmetic; `to_csv` to save **Next session:** data quality — what to do when the file is not clean. ## Practice at home (~1 h) - load a table from your own work (CSV or Excel) with pandas, run the 5 checks - write down anything that went wrong — we start Session 7 with your examples
